- If sentiment is positive (≥0.20) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is falling, avoid sharp declines — model should show slight mean reversion or pause.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 90), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00) and history shows volatility, forecast should be tighter (smaller std dev) and avoid long-term linear trends.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 89→82→85), model should adjust downward early — don’t wait for 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >90 and true outcome drops below 85, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.20 spikes, model should not assume continuation — expect correction within 3–5 days.  
- When true outcome is volatile (e.g., 89→82→85→88), forecast should be more adaptive — avoid rigid linear extrapolation.  
- If forecast is flat (±0.1) and true outcome moves >1.5% in 3 days, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift.  
- For sentiment history with 0.00 for 3+ days, forecast should not be overly bullish — expect 1–2% downward bias unless new catalysts appear.
